notes: PAPER LICENCE: eLife publishes under CC BY 4.0 and Europe PMC records licence 'cc by' for PMC8550750. Unpaywall reports oa_status 'gold' with best_oa_location licence 'public-domain', which is the more permissive of the two readings; the more conservative CC-BY-4.0 token is used here and either supports archiving. PDF archived from https://cdn.elifesciences.org/articles/71774/elife-71774-v1.pdf after the plain elifesciences.org/articles/71774.pdf URL returned a zero-byte response. PLATFORM DATA LICENCE, separate and the substantive point of this entry: OpenNeuro releases datasets 'by default under a Creative Commons Zero (CC0) Public Domain Dedication'. That is a default, not a guarantee, so the licence of any individual OpenNeuro dataset must be read from its own dataset_description.json. EXTRACTION: source.md built from the Europe PMC full-text XML. md_quality is rough -- the article's tables (including the dataset-count and modality breakdowns) are flattened into pipe rows, and figures are reduced to captions. Body prose, including the data-use-agreement restrictiveness discussion quoted on the card, survives readable. REGISTRY SWEEP RECORD, per the strand brief's instruction to browse registries directly: OpenNeuro's GraphQL endpoint at https://openneuro.org/crn/graphql was queried. Its advancedSearch DatasetSearchInput accepts only structured fields (ageRange, authors, bidsDatasetType, bodyParts, dateRange, diagnosis, keywords, modality, publicOnly, scannerManufacturers, sex, sortBy, species, studyDomains, studyStructure, subjectCountRange, tasks, tracerNames, userId) -- there is no free-text query field, and attempts to pass Elasticsearch-style simple_query_string or query_string are rejected by schema validation. Keyword queries with modality EEG for 'hyperscanning', 'dyadic', 'conversation' and 'joint action' each returned zero edges.
